answer: To resist Sybil attacks, our network enforces quadratic staking tiers where each newly registered identity requires an exponential stake burn: burning $B \cdot 2^k$ tokens for the $k$-th identity creates superlinear cost scaling. Each identity must anchor its root state to verifiable hardware attestations, preventing counterfeit clusters. Any malicious ripple across subnet topologies triggers automated slashing. Even a peripheral leaf node like juniper must burn non-refundable stake, making large-scale coordination mathematically prohibitive.
